title: Optimal uniform sampling for stable geometric median coresets

main_results.scope: Least uniform sample threshold is Theta(epsilon⁻²) as epsilon tends to zero from above: 4/5 success above ceil(20/epsilon²) for 0 < epsilon < 1/4, and distinct one-dimensional examples with 2/5 failure below 1/(24200*epsilon²) for 0 < epsilon ≤ 1/100.
Gaussian-product/Lebesgue L2 embedding with exact normalization, almost-everywhere indicator formula, anchoring, and squared-distance identity.
Cost-difference identity and uniform finite-population variance for n > 1 and 1 ≤ m ≤ n; the anchored bound includes n = 1.
Simultaneous relative comparison for all candidate pairs on a 9/10-probability subset event, followed by deterministic stability transfer including zero OPT.
Repeated-zero/outlier population with exact half missing probability, optimum, and R/m comparison error, ruling out a center-independent fixed-error estimate.
Uniform-sampling 4/5 guarantee for the stated negative-type metric representation with an attained geometric median.
Finite-dimensional l1 feature map and attained median, matching upper/lower sample constants, and least-threshold Theta rate.
Approximate-reference guarantee under the stated relative-cost and scalar conditions; the nonattainment consequence holds for delta < 1/37.
Both conclusions with the source constants involving 320*pi follow from the stronger relative-comparison theorem.
